## Benchmark Methodology

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/benchmarks/methodology

Summary: Scientific benchmarking harness, dataset composition, and measurement standards for evaluating web extraction engines.

To provide objective, reproducible comparisons between Atlas and alternative web extraction tools, we evaluated execution performance, token efficiency, table fidelity, and memory overhead across a diverse corpus of **1,000 production websites**.

---

## Dataset Composition (Atlas-1000)

The **Atlas-1000 Corpus** consists of real-world URLs selected across 5 distinct web architecture categories:

| Category | Count | Characteristics | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Complex SPAs & Web Apps** | 250 | Heavy client-side hydration, client-side routing, skeleton screens, dynamic shadow DOM. | Linear, Twitter/X, Vercel, Supabase |
| **Technical Documentation** | 250 | Multi-level navigation trees, code fences with syntax highlighting, tabs, callout boxes. | Stripe, Next.js, GitHub Docs, AWS |
| **Financial & Pricing Tables** | 200 | Multi-column comparison matrices, sticky headers, tooltips, currency toggles. | OpenAI, AWS Pricing, Shopify, Datadog |
| **News, Publications & Media** | 150 | Heavy advertising banners, cookie consent dialogs, related article sidebars, dynamic video players. | NYTimes, The Verge, Bloomberg, TechCrunch |
| **E-Commerce & Catalogs** | 150 | Faceted search, pagination, product variant grids, customer review carousels. | Amazon, Shopify stores, Target |

---

## Evaluation Metrics

### 1. Latency & Time-to-First-Chunk (TTFC)
We measure total roundtrip wall-clock time from the client's initial request until the full compiled Markdown or AST payload is received. We record **P50 (Median)**, **P90**, and **P99** latencies across 10 consecutive cold-start and warm-cache runs.

### 2. Token Tax Reduction
For every web page, we compute the token count using OpenAI's `o200k_base` (GPT-4o) and `cl100k_base` (GPT-4) tokenizers:
$$\text{Token Tax Reduction \%} = \frac{\text{Raw HTML Tokens} - \text{Atlas Markdown Tokens}}{\text{Raw HTML Tokens}} \times 100$$

### 3. Table Structural Fidelity (TSF Score)
Table fidelity measures whether tabular data in the DOM is accurately reconstructed in GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) pipe tables without scrambled columns or collapsed multi-line cells. Graded from 0% (total failure/missing) to 100% (perfect row/column alignment).

### 4. Server Resource Footprint (RAM & CPU)
We profile resident set size (RSS) memory consumption and CPU cycle duration required to compile each page under identical 100-request concurrent loads.

---

## Testing Environment & Reproducibility

- **Hardware**: Dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor (2.45 GHz), 256 GB RAM, 10 Gbps symmetric network uplink.
- **Client Runner**: Node.js v22 test runner executing parallel requests with 10-second request timeouts and randomized target order.
- **Comparison Baselines**:
  - **Headless Chromium (Puppeteer/Playwright)**: Full browser automation with network idle wait conditions.
  - **Naive DOM Parsers (Readability.js + Turndown)**: Standard open-source heuristic readability algorithms.
  - **Atlas Web Compiler**: Native edge pipeline with visual tree analysis.

---

## Atlas Arena Results

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/benchmarks/atlas-arena-results

Summary: Empirical benchmark results evaluating Atlas against Headless Chromium, Readability.js, and legacy web scraping tools.

The results below reflect the audited run of the **Atlas-1000 Benchmark Corpus** (September 2026), evaluating Atlas against industry baselines across latency, token savings, table fidelity, and memory efficiency.

---

## Executive Summary

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph LatencyGroup ["P50 Latency (Lower is Better)"]
        Atlas["Atlas: 1,308ms"]
        Readability["Readability.js: 980ms"]
        Puppeteer["Headless Chrome: 4,820ms"]
    end
```

- **3.7x Faster than Headless Chrome**: Atlas completes full SPA and document compilation in **1,308ms (P50)** vs **4,820ms** for Puppeteer/Playwright.
- **65% Average Token Tax Reduction**: By stripping irrelevant navigation chrome, ads, and boilerplate code, Atlas saves an average of 65% of context window tokens per page.
- **98.4% Table Accuracy**: Complex multi-column pricing and financial tables are converted into aligned GFM pipe tables with 98.4% fidelity (vs 42.1% for naive HTML-to-Markdown parsers).
- **40x Less Memory Overhead**: Atlas executes within a lightweight isolate consuming **` documentation body, collapses tabbed snippets into distinct language-tagged code blocks, and preserves heading hierarchy (`#`, `##`, `###`).
- **Readability.js**: Frequently strips code blocks or mistakes navigation breadcrumbs for body content.
- **Result**: **71.4% token reduction** with 100% code block accuracy.

---

### 2. Pricing & Financial Matrices (SaaS Pricing, SEC Filings)
Dynamic pricing grids often use CSS grid or flexbox layouts with sticky header columns.
- **Atlas**: Uses geometric layout analysis to map CSS column alignments into standard Markdown pipe tables (`| Tier | Monthly | Features |`).
- **Readability.js**: Discards CSS layout data, outputting unstructured paragraphs where feature checkmarks are separated from their column headers.
- **Result**: **98.4% table structural fidelity**, enabling zero-hallucination analysis in LLMs.

---

### 3. Single-Page Applications (Linear, Twitter/X, Supabase)
SPAs deliver empty `` shells on initial HTTP download.
- **Atlas**: Executes client JavaScript within isolated execution engines, waiting for DOM mutation stability before compiling the visual tree.
- **Readability.js**: Returns 0 words of body content (complete extraction failure).
- **Result**: **100% extraction success** on modern client-side apps without running heavy Chromium binaries.

## REST API Overview

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/overview

Summary: Core conventions, authentication, base URLs, rate limits, and idempotency headers for the Atlas public REST API.

The Atlas REST API provides programmatic, low-latency access to the Atlas web compiler, visual Markdown extractor, sitemap crawler, and topology mapper.

The API is structured around REST principles, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns standard HTTP response codes, and delivers RFC 9457 machine-readable error responses.

---

## Base URL

All requests must be made over HTTPS to the production API origin:

```http
https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1
```

  Workspace resolution is automatic. When you authenticate using a Bearer API key, Atlas automatically associates the request with your target workspace and default project without requiring manual workspace path parameters.

---

## Authentication

Every request to the Atlas API requires a valid API key passed in the standard HTTP `Authorization` header:

Requests missing the `Authorization` header or presenting an expired or revoked key receive an immediate `401 Unauthorized` response.

---

## Idempotency & Safe Retries

For mutating endpoints (such as `POST /v1/compile`, `POST /v1/crawls`, and `POST /v1/batches`), you can attach an optional `Idempotency-Key` header:

When you supply an `Idempotency-Key`:
- If an identical request is received within 24 hours while the previous request was already processed, Atlas returns the cached result with an added HTTP header: `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
- If an identical request arrives while the first request is still actively executing, Atlas safely coordinates execution to prevent duplicate work or redundant billing deductions.

---

## Request & Response Headers

### Standard Request Headers

| Header | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Authorization` | **Yes** | Bearer authentication token (`Bearer atlas_...`). |
| `Content-Type` | **Yes** | Must be `application/json` for all POST requests. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | No | Unique client-generated key (min 8 chars) for retry deduplication. |

### Standard Response Headers

Every response from the Atlas API includes headers for tracing, rate limiting, and caching:

| Header | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `x-atlas-request-id` | Unique request identifier (e.g., `req_01j7abc123...`) used for support and tracing. |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` | Maximum number of requests allowed per rolling minute for your tier. |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` | Remaining request quota available in the current rate limit window. |
| `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` | Seconds remaining until the current rate limit window resets. |
| `Idempotency-Replayed` | Present and set to `"true"` when returning a previously computed response. |

---

## Standard HTTP Status Codes

Atlas uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate request outcomes:

| Status Code | Meaning | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `200 OK` | Success | The compilation or operation completed synchronously. The response body contains results. |
| `202 Accepted` | Asynchronous Job | Long-running crawls or batches have been queued. Inspect the returned `Location` header or job ID. |
| `400 Bad Request` | Validation Error | Request body or query parameters failed validation. Details appear in `invalidParams`. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Authentication Failure | Missing, malformed, or invalid API key. |
| `403 Forbidden` | Access Denied | API key lacks required scope, or IP address is not allowlisted. |
| `404 Not Found` | Resource Missing | Target job ID, workspace, or resource does not exist. |
| `409 Conflict` | State Conflict | An in-flight idempotent request is conflicting, or resource state is locked. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate Limit Exceeded | Workspace exceeded concurrent job limits or per-minute request rate. Inspect `retryAfter`. |
| `500 Internal Error` | Internal Server Error | Unexpected error occurred in the edge cluster. Request is automatically marked retryable. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Service Unavailable | Engine capacity temporary saturation or scheduled maintenance window. |

For detailed machine-readable error codes and handling recipes, see the [RFC 9457 Error Dictionary](/api-reference/errors).

---

## Polyglot Quick Example

Here is how to perform an authenticated synchronous extraction across our 4 supported SDK languages:

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }'
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({
  apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY!,
});

const result = await atlas.scrape({
  url: 'https://example.com',
  formats: ['markdown'],
});

console.log(result.data.markdown);
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

result = atlas.scrape(
    url="https://example.com",
    formats=["markdown"],
)

print(result.data.markdown)
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	result, _, err := client.Scrape(context.Background(), atlas.ScrapeUrlRequest{
		Url: "https://example.com",
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	if result.Data.Markdown != nil {
		fmt.Println(*result.Data.Markdown)
	}
}
```

---

## Asynchronous operations & webhooks

Long-running jobs—such as recursive domain crawls (`POST /v1/crawls`) and multi-URL batches (`POST /v1/batches`)—execute asynchronously.

When submitted, Atlas immediately returns `HTTP 202 Accepted` with a unique job ID (`job_...`). You can track progress in two ways:

1. **Webhooks (Recommended)**: Pass an HTTPS `webhook` parameter in your request body to receive real-time push notifications when the job reaches terminal completion (`job.ready`, `job.failed`, `job.cancelled`) or as individual crawl pages complete (`crawl.page_completed`). See the [Webhooks Guide](/guides/webhooks) for event schemas, replay protection, and signature verification.
2. **Polling**: Query `GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}` until `status` transitions to `ready` or `failed`, or use the built-in `waitForJob` polling helper provided by the official SDKs.

---

## RFC 9457 Error Dictionary

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/errors

Summary: Machine-readable Problem Details schema, comprehensive error code dictionary, and resilient programmatic handling recipes.

Atlas returns errors formatted according to the **RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs** specification (`Content-Type: application/problem+json`).

Every error response contains a stable, machine-readable `code`, human-readable `detail`, HTTP status code, a unique tracing `requestId`, and an explicit boolean `retryable` indicator so your application can make deterministic retry decisions without fragile regex string parsing.

---

## Error Response Schema

### Problem Details Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `type` | `string` | **Yes** | An absolute URI reference that identifies the problem type. |
| `title` | `string` | **Yes** | A short, human-readable summary of the problem type. |
| `status` | `integer` | **Yes** | The HTTP status code generated by the origin server. |
| `detail` | `string` | **Yes** | A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem. |
| `instance` | `string` | **Yes** | The request URI path where the problem occurred. |
| `requestId` | `string` | **Yes** | Unique request trace ID (e.g., `req_01j7abc123...`). Always provide this ID to Atlas support. |
| `code` | `string` | **Yes** | A snake_case machine-readable error code for client switch/case statements. |
| `retryable` | `boolean` | **Yes** | When `true`, the client may safely retry the request using exponential backoff. |
| `documentationUrl` | `string` | No | Direct link to the public documentation troubleshooting guide for this specific error code. |
| `invalidParams` | `object[]` | No | List of parameter validation errors, containing `name` and `reason` pairs. |

---

## Complete Error Code Reference

### 1. Authentication & Authorization Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `unauthorized` | `401` | No | Missing `Authorization` header or malformed Bearer token. Check API key presence. |
| `invalid_credentials` | `401` | No | API key is revoked, expired, or invalid. Verify in the Atlas Dashboard. |
| `forbidden` | `403` | No | Caller lacks permission or token lacks the required scope (e.g. `atlas:crawl`). |
| `workspace_not_found` | `404` | No | The workspace associated with the credentials could not be located or is deleted. |
| `forbidden_origin` | `403` | No | MCP client origin header is disallowed (browser DNS rebinding defense). |
| `forbidden_host` | `403` | No | Host header mismatch during MCP connection. |

---

### 2. Validation & Request Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `validation_failed` | `400` | No | Request body failed schema validation. Inspect `invalidParams` for field-level errors. |
| `bad_request` | `400` | No | Malformed JSON payload or unsupported parameters. |
| `invalid_cursor` | `400` | No | Pagination cursor has expired, is corrupted, or was generated with different parameters. |
| `invalid_workspace_slug` | `400` | No | Provided workspace slug does not conform to URL-safe naming constraints. |

---

### 3. Concurrency & Idempotency Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `idempotency_conflict` | `409` | Yes | An identical request is currently executing in-flight. Wait 500ms and retry with the same key. |
| `conflict` | `409` | No | Target resource was modified or is currently in an incompatible state. |

---

### 4. Quotas & Billing Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `rate_limited` | `429` | Yes | Request rate exceeded per-minute capacity. Back off according to `retryAfter`. |
| `plan_limit_exceeded` | `429` | No | Workspace reached maximum concurrent jobs allowed for its plan tier. |
| `insufficient_credits` | `402` | No | Balance is lower than required operation cost. Top up credits in the Atlas Dashboard. |
| `credits_exhausted` | `402` | No | Credit balance has reached zero. All compilation operations are halted. |

---

### 5. Upstream Target Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `upstream_fetch_failed` | `502` | Yes | Target web server returned a 5xx error or dropped the connection. |
| `upstream_timeout` | `504` | Yes | Target web server failed to respond within the execution timeout (default: 30s). |
| `upstream_dns_failure` | `502` | No | Target domain does not exist or failed DNS resolution. |
| `upstream_blocked` | `502` | No | Target IP is private or restricted by SSRF protection filters. |

---

### 6. Infrastructure Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Retryable | Cause & Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `service_unavailable` | `503` | Yes | Edge cluster capacity is momentarily saturated. Safe to retry with exponential backoff. |
| `internal_error` | `500` | Yes | Unexpected unhandled exception in the edge pipeline. Contact support with `requestId`. |

---

## Programmatic Error Handling Recipes

Use the `retryable` field and machine-readable `code` to build resilient client applications:

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY! });

async function compileWithRetry(url: string, maxRetries = 3) {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt  setTimeout(resolve, delay));
          continue;
        }
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
}
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient, AtlasError

atlas = AtlasClient()

def compile_with_retry(url: str, max_retries: int = 3):
    for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return atlas.compile(url=url)
        except AtlasError as err:
            print(f"Atlas Error [{err.code}]: {err.message} (Request ID: {err.request_id})")

            if err.code == "validation_failed":
                raise  # Permanent failure

            if err.retryable and attempt = maxRetries {
				return result, err
			}

			delay := time.Duration(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))*500+float64(rand.Intn(200))) * time.Millisecond
			time.Sleep(delay)
			continue
		}

		return result, err
	}
	var empty atlas.CompileUrlResult
	return empty, errors.New("exceeded maximum retries")
}
```

---

## Response Structure

A successful `200 OK` response contains:
- `data.markdown`: LLM-ready clean Markdown.
- `data.links`: Extracted outbound hyperlinks with anchored text.
- `metadata`: Page title, canonical URL, HTTP status code, and extraction timestamp.
- `usage.credits`: Number of credits deducted for the compilation (default: 1 credit).

Execute a visual compilation against a target URL. The Atlas compiler analyzes DOM geometry, computes visual bounding boxes, strips ads and navigation noise, and emits clean GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) pipe tables and syntax-highlighted code blocks.

## Asynchronous Execution

For complex web pages requiring extended rendering, Atlas may return `202 Accepted` with an admitted job descriptor:

```json
{
  "id": "job_01j7abc...",
  "status": "queued",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-19T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

When receiving `202 Accepted`, poll the status using [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}`](/api-reference/get-job) until `status` becomes `"ready"`.

## Map Domain

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/map
API Operation: POST /v1/map
Summary: Discover URL topology, sitemaps, and linked navigation graphs for an entire domain without downloading page bodies.

Discover the structural architecture of a domain. Atlas inspects `robots.txt`, traverses standard and nested XML sitemaps, and follows high-priority internal links to return a prioritized list of available URLs.

---

## Authentication & Headers

---

## Code Examples

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/map \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://docs.github.com",
    "limit": 50,
    "sitemap": "include",
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }'
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY });

const result = await atlas.map({
  url: 'https://docs.github.com',
  limit: 50,
  sitemap: 'include',
  includeSubdomains: false,
});

if (result.status === 200) {
  console.log(`Discovered ${result.value.links.length} URLs (Estimated total: ${result.value.summary.estimatedPages}):`);
  result.value.links.forEach((link) => console.log(` - [Priority ${link.priority}] ${link.url}`));
}
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

client = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

result = client.map({
    "url": "https://docs.github.com",
    "limit": 50,
    "sitemap": "include",
    "includeSubdomains": False,
})

if result.status == 200:
    links = result.value["links"]
    print(f"Discovered {len(links)} URLs (Estimated total: {result.value['summary']['estimatedPages']}):")
    for link in links:
        print(f" - [Priority {link['priority']}] {link['url']}")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	limit := 50
	sitemap := "include"
	subdomains := false

	res, _, err := client.Map(context.Background(), atlas.MapUrlRequest{
		Url:               "https://docs.github.com",
		Limit:             &limit,
		Sitemap:           &sitemap,
		IncludeSubdomains: &subdomains,
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	if res.Response200 != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Discovered %d URLs (Estimated total: %d)\n", len(res.Response200.Links), res.Response200.Summary.EstimatedPages)
		for _, link := range res.Response200.Links {
			fmt.Printf(" - [Priority %v] %s\n", link.Priority, link.Url)
		}
	}
}
```

---

## Response Structure

A successful `200 OK` response contains:
- `success`: Boolean indicating whether mapping completed successfully.
- `links`: Array of discovered URL objects:
  - `url`: Discovered page URL.
  - `title`: Extracted page title (if available from navigation or sitemap).
  - `description`: Meta description or extracted snippet summary.
  - `sources`: Discovery origins (`["sitemap"]`, `["homepage"]`, `["navigation"]`, `["rss"]`, `["manifest"]`).
  - `priority`: Normalized relevance score (0–100).
  - `confidence`: Heuristic certainty score (0–100).
  - `depth`: Link depth relative to the root URL.
  - `recommended`: Boolean indicating high-priority content recommended for indexing or compilation.
  - `incomingLinks`: Number of internal pages linking to this route.
- `summary`: High-level domain topology metrics:
  - `estimatedPages`: Estimated total page count across the domain.
  - `framework`: Detected web framework (e.g. Next.js, Astro, Docusaurus).
  - `language`: Detected primary language.
  - `discoveryConfidence`: Discovery confidence percentage.
  - `recommendedDepth`: Recommended crawl depth limit.
  - `recommendedEntryPoint`: Primary documentation or content entry route.
  - `estimatedCompileTime`: Estimated time to compile the mapped pages.
  - `estimatedTokens`: Estimated token count for LLM context planning.
- `usage`: Credit consumption details (`credits: 1`).

---

## Create Crawl Job

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/crawl
API Operation: POST /v1/crawls
Summary: Start a distributed, recursive crawl across an entire domain or documentation section.

Initiate a distributed, asynchronous crawl job across a target website. Atlas traverses hyperlinks from the root URL, enforces inclusion/exclusion path rules, respects sitemaps, and compiles discovered pages into clean Markdown.

---

## Authentication & Headers

To prevent duplicate crawl jobs on accidental retries, provide an `Idempotency-Key` header:

---

## Code Examples

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/crawls \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 01JCRAWLJOB001" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://docs.stripe.com",
    "maxPages": 100,
    "maxDepth": 5,
    "includePaths": ["/docs/**"],
    "excludePaths": ["/docs/legacy/**"]
  }'
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY! });

const res = await atlas.createCrawl({
  url: 'https://docs.stripe.com',
  maxPages: 100,
  maxDepth: 5,
  includePaths: ['/docs/**'],
  excludePaths: ['/docs/legacy/**'],
  webhook: {
    url: 'https://api.your-domain.com/webhooks/atlas',
    events: ['job.ready', 'job.failed'],
  },
});

console.log('Crawl Job Admitted:', res.value.id);
console.log('Status:', res.value.status);
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

res = atlas.create_crawl({
    "url": "https://docs.stripe.com",
    "maxPages": 100,
    "maxDepth": 5,
    "includePaths": ["/docs/**"],
    "excludePaths": ["/docs/legacy/**"],
    "webhook": "https://api.your-domain.com/webhooks/atlas",
})

print(f"Crawl Job Admitted: {res.value['id']} (Status: {res.value['status']})")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	maxPages := 100
	maxDepth := 5
	res, _, err := client.CreateCrawl(context.Background(), atlas.CreateCrawlRequest{
		Url:          "https://docs.stripe.com",
		MaxPages:     &maxPages,
		MaxDepth:     &maxDepth,
		IncludePaths: []string{"/docs/**"},
		ExcludePaths: []string{"/docs/legacy/**"},
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	fmt.Printf("Crawl Job Admitted: %s (Status: %s)\n", res.Response202.Id, res.Response202.Status)
}
```

---

## Asynchronous Lifecycle & Polling

When a crawl is admitted, Atlas returns `202 Accepted` with a `Location: /v1/jobs/{jobId}` header and an initial job object:

```json
{
  "id": "job_01j7abc...",
  "status": "queued",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-19T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Retrieving Results

1. **Poll Status**: Call [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}`](/api-reference/get-job) periodically until `status` transitions to `"ready"` or `"failed"`.
2. **Fetch Pages**: Once ready, fetch compiled page artifacts using cursor pagination via [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/results`](/api-reference/job-results).
3. **Inspect Errors**: Any individual page errors encountered during the crawl are accessible via [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/errors`](/api-reference/job-errors).

---

## Create Batch Job

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/batch
API Operation: POST /v1/batches
Summary: Submit multi-URL batch compilation requests with parallel execution and isolated partial failure handling.

Submit a batch of up to 1,000 URLs for parallel compilation. Atlas distributes the batch across its edge cluster, compiles pages concurrently, and isolates upstream errors so that failure on one URL does not prevent others from succeeding.

---

## Authentication & Headers

To prevent duplicate batch creation on network retries, provide an `Idempotency-Key` header:

---

```bash cURL
    "urls": [
      "https://example.com/page-1",
      "https://example.com/page-2",
      "https://example.com/page-3"
    ],
    "formats": ["markdown", "links"]
  }'
```

```typescript TypeScript

    events: ['job.ready', 'job.failed'],
  },
});

console.log('Batch Job Created:', res.value.id);
console.log('Status:', res.value.status);
```

```python Python
})
```


---

## Tracking Progress & Fetching Results

Atlas admits the batch job asynchronously, returning `202 Accepted` with the job descriptor:

1. **Poll Status**: Call [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}`](/api-reference/get-job) to monitor `progress.completedItems` and `progress.failedItems`.
2. **Retrieve Results**: Once complete, stream or paginate the compiled documents via [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/results`](/api-reference/job-results).
3. **Inspect Errors**: Any failed URLs can be inspected via [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/errors`](/api-reference/job-errors).

---

## Get Job Status

API Operation: GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}
Summary: Retrieve execution status, lifecycle progression, item counters, and artifact readiness for any asynchronous job.

Inspect the current status and execution lifecycle of an asynchronous job (such as a crawl, batch compile, or deferred compilation).

```python Python
res = client.get_job("job_01j7abc123")
job = res.value

print(f"Status: {job['status']}")
if job.get("progress"):
    print(f"Progress: {job['progress']['completedItems']} completed, {job['progress']['queuedItems']} queued")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	job, _, err := client.GetJob(context.Background(), "job_01j7abc123")
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	fmt.Printf("Status: %s\n", job.Status)
	if job.Progress != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Completed: %d, Queued: %d\n", job.Progress.CompletedItems, job.Progress.QueuedItems)
	}
}
```

---

## Job Lifecycle States

Jobs transition through the following state machine:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Queued["queued"] --> Running["running"]
    Running --> Ingesting["ingesting"]
    Ingesting --> Ready["ready (Complete)"]
    Running --> Failed["failed"]
    Queued --> Cancelled["cancelled"]
    Running --> Cancelled
```

| Status | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `queued` | Job has been admitted and is awaiting cluster execution slot. |
| `running` | Pages are actively being fetched, rendered, and compiled across edge nodes. |
| `ingesting` | All pages compiled; artifacts and indexes are finalizing. |
| `ready` | Terminal success state. Compiled pages are ready for retrieval via [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/results`](/api-reference/job-results). |
| `failed` | Unrecoverable error occurred. Check [`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/errors`](/api-reference/job-errors). |
| `cancelled` | Execution was explicitly halted by a user cancellation request. |

---

## Get Job Results

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/job-results
API Operation: GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/results
Summary: Retrieve paginated results and compiled page artifacts for an asynchronous crawl, compile, or batch job.

Fetch compiled page artifacts for an asynchronous crawl or batch job. Results are delivered using opaque cursor-based pagination to guarantee consistent ordering across high-volume crawls.

---

## Authentication & Headers

---

## Code Examples

```bash cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/jobs/job_01j7abc123/results?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY"
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY });

const results = await atlas.listJobResults('job_01j7abc123', {
  limit: 20,
});

for (const item of results.value.data) {
  console.log('URL:', item.url);
  console.log('Markdown:\n', item.markdown);
}

if (results.value.nextCursor) {
  console.log('Next Cursor:', results.value.nextCursor);
}
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

client = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

results = client.list_job_results("job_01j7abc123", limit=20)

for item in results.value["data"]:
    print(f"URL: {item['url']}")
    print(item["markdown"][:200])

if results.value.get("nextCursor"):
    print(f"Next Cursor: {results.value['nextCursor']}")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	limit := 20
	results, _, err := client.ListJobResults(context.Background(), "job_01j7abc123", nil, &limit)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	for _, item := range results.Data {
		if item.Url != nil {
			fmt.Printf("URL: %s\n", *item.Url)
		}
	}

	if results.NextCursor != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Next Cursor: %s\n", *results.NextCursor)
	}
}
```

---

## Pagination Pattern

When iterating through large crawl jobs (e.g. 5,000 pages), supply the `nextCursor` value from the previous response in the `cursor` query parameter until `nextCursor` is `null` or omitted:

```http
GET /v1/jobs/job_01j7abc123/results?limit=50&cursor=cur_01j8xyz...
```

---

## Get Job Errors

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/job-errors
API Operation: GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/errors
Summary: Retrieve URL-level failure diagnostics, upstream status codes, and error categories for an asynchronous job.

Inspect individual URL failures and execution diagnostics for an asynchronous crawl or batch compilation job.

Because Atlas employs partial failure isolation, individual target page failures (such as a 404, 500 upstream server error, or network timeout) do not terminate the parent job. Use this endpoint to inspect failed items and diagnose upstream target issues.

---

## Authentication & Headers

---

## Code Examples

```bash cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/jobs/job_01j7abc123/errors?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY"
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY });

const errors = await atlas.listJobErrors('job_01j7abc123', {
  limit: 20,
});

for (const err of errors.value.data) {
  console.error(`Failed: ${err.url} -> [${err.code}] ${err.detail}`);
}
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

client = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

errors = client.list_job_errors("job_01j7abc123", limit=20)

for err in errors.value["data"]:
    print(f"Failed: {err['url']} -> [{err['code']}] {err['detail']}")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	limit := 20
	errors, _, err := client.ListJobErrors(context.Background(), "job_01j7abc123", nil, &limit)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	for _, e := range errors.Data {
		url := ""
		if e.Url != nil {
			url = *e.Url
		}
		fmt.Printf("Failed: %s -> [%s] %s\n", url, e.Code, e.Detail)
	}
}
```

---

## Common Error Diagnostics

Individual failed items in `errors.data` include:
- `id`: Unique error record identifier (`artifact_...`).
- `url`: The target URL that could not be compiled.
- `code`: RFC 9457 error code (e.g. `upstream_timeout`, `upstream_fetch_failed`, `unsupported_content_type`).
- `detail`: Diagnostic description of why compilation failed.
- `occurredAt`: ISO 8601 timestamp when the failure occurred.

---

## Cancel Job

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/api-reference/cancel-job
API Operation: DELETE /v1/jobs/{jobId}
Summary: Cancel an in-flight asynchronous crawl, batch compilation, or long-running execution.

Immediately requests cancellation of an active asynchronous job. When cancelled, Atlas terminates in-flight execution on edge nodes, prevents remaining queued items from running, and marks the job status as `"cancelled"`.

---

## Authentication & Headers

Cancellation requires an `Idempotency-Key` header:

---

## Code Examples

```bash cURL
curl -X DELETE https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/jobs/job_01j7abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLAS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 01JCANCEL001"
```

```typescript TypeScript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY });

const result = await atlas.cancelJob('job_01j7abc123');

console.log('Cancellation Accepted:', result.value.accepted);
console.log('Job Status:', result.value.job.status);
```

```python Python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

client = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

result = client.cancel_job("job_01j7abc123")

print(f"Cancellation Accepted: {result.value['accepted']}")
print(f"Job Status: {result.value['job']['status']}")
```

```go Go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	result, _, err := client.CancelJob(context.Background(), "job_01j7abc123")
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	fmt.Printf("Cancellation Accepted: %t\n", result.Accepted)
	fmt.Printf("Job Status: %s\n", result.Job.Status)
}
```

---

## Response

Returns `202 Accepted` indicating that the cancellation signal has been received and dispatched across cluster nodes:

```json
{
  "accepted": true,
  "job": {
    "id": "job_01j7abc123",
    "status": "cancelled",
    "cancellationRequestedAt": "2026-09-19T12:05:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

## SDK Overview

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/sdk/overview

Summary: Official, type-safe client libraries for TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, and Go with automatic workspace resolution and retry resilience.

Atlas provides official, contract-tested client libraries for **TypeScript/JavaScript**, **Python**, and **Go**. Every SDK is generated directly from reviewed OpenAPI specifications, guaranteeing 100% schema alignment with the production Atlas API.

---

## Available SDKs

  
  

---

## Core design principles

All official Atlas SDKs follow consistent architectural standards:

1. **Automatic workspace resolution**: Authenticate using your Atlas API key (`atlas_...`). The SDK and backend resolve your workspace and default project automatically.
2. **Type safety & schema fidelity**: Request parameters, responses, metadata, and error objects are strongly typed according to our public OpenAPI contracts.
3. **Built-in resilience & exponential backoff**: Transient errors (HTTP 429 rate limits, 503 capacity saturation) are automatically retried with jitter when marked retryable.
4. **Idempotency built-in**: Mutating compilation, crawl, and batch requests accept client-provided idempotency keys to ensure zero-duplicate billing on retries.
5. **Zero external dependencies**: Our TypeScript library runs anywhere modern JavaScript executes (Node.js 18+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js Edge).

---

## SDK feature support matrix

| Feature | TypeScript / JavaScript | Python | Go |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Synchronous Scrape & Compile** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **Domain Topology Mapping** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **Distributed Crawls & Batches** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **Cursor-based Pagination** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **RFC 9457 Problem Errors** | Supported (`AtlasError`) | Supported (`AtlasError`) | Supported (`atlas.Error`) |
| **Standard Webhooks Verification** | Supported (`verifyWebhookSignature`) | Supported (`verify_webhook_signature`) | Supported (`atlas.VerifyWebhook`) |
| **Dual-Secret Rotation Support** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **Automatic Retries with Jitter** | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| **Streaming / Raw Operations** | Supported (`client.raw()`) | Supported (`client.raw()`) | Supported |

---

The official `@atlascompiler/sdk` provides a lightweight, fully typed interface for interacting with the Atlas REST API. It uses the web standard `fetch` API, contains zero runtime dependencies, and works across Node.js 18+, Bun, Deno, and edge environments.

## Initialization

Initialize the `AtlasClient`. If no API key is passed in options, the client automatically reads from the `ATLAS_API_KEY` environment variable:

```typescript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({
  apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY, // Optional if set in environment
  timeout: 30000,                    // Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 30s)
});
```

---

## Core Operations

### 1. Scrape a URL

Synchronously extract clean Markdown and links from a single page:

```typescript
const result = await atlas.scrape({
  url: 'https://news.ycombinator.com',
  formats: ['markdown', 'links'],
});

console.log(result.value.metadata.title);
console.log(result.value.data.markdown);
```

---

### 2. Compile a Dynamic Page or SPA

Execute visual DOM compilation preserving multi-column tables and code fences:

```typescript
const result = await atlas.compile({
  url: 'https://stripe.com/pricing',
  cache: { forceFresh: false },
});

if (result.status === 200) {
  console.log('Markdown:\n', result.value.markdown);
  console.log('Credits Used:', result.value.usage.credits);
}
```

---

### 3. Map Domain Topology

Map sitemaps and site architecture without downloading page bodies:

```typescript
const mapResult = await atlas.map({
  url: 'https://docs.github.com',
  limit: 100,
  sitemap: 'include',
});

if (mapResult.status === 200) {
  console.log(`Discovered ${mapResult.value.links.length} URLs:`);
  mapResult.value.links.forEach((link) => console.log(' -', link.url));
}
```

---

### 4. Create and Monitor a Crawl Job

Start an asynchronous multi-page crawl with path filtering:

```typescript
// 1. Create crawl job
const res = await atlas.createCrawl({
  url: 'https://docs.stripe.com',
  maxPages: 50,
  maxDepth: 3,
  includePaths: ['/docs/**'],
  excludePaths: ['/docs/legacy/**'],
});

const jobId = res.value.id;
console.log('Crawl admitted:', jobId);

// 2. Poll for completion using built-in helper
const job = await atlas.waitForJob(jobId);

// 3. Fetch compiled pages
if (job.status === 'ready') {
  const pages = await atlas.listJobResults(jobId, { limit: 50 });
  for (const item of pages.value.data) {
    console.log(item.url, '->', item.markdown?.slice(0, 100));
  }
}
```

---

## Error Handling

All API errors throw typed `AtlasError` instances compliant with RFC 9457:

```typescript

const atlas = new AtlasClient();

try {
  await atlas.compile({ url: 'https://invalid-domain.example' });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof AtlasError) {
    console.error(`Status: ${err.status}`);
    console.error(`Error Code: ${err.code}`);
    console.error(`Detail: ${err.message}`);
    console.error(`Request ID: ${err.requestId}`);
    console.error(`Retryable: ${err.retryable}`);
  }
}
```

---

## Verifying webhook signatures

The SDK exports `verifyWebhookSignature` to authenticate incoming Standard Webhooks requests from Atlas using HMAC-SHA256:

```typescript

// In an Express, Next.js API route, or Hono handler:
const result = await verifyWebhookSignature({
  payload: req.rawBody, // raw body string or Uint8Array
  headers: req.headers, // Node.js req.headers or Web Standard Headers
  secret: process.env.ATLAS_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  previousSecret: process.env.ATLAS_OLD_WEBHOOK_SECRET, // Optional 24h rotation support
  toleranceSeconds: 300,                               // 5-minute replay window (default: 300)
});

if (!result.valid) {
  console.error('Webhook verification rejected:', result.error);
  return res.status(401).send('Unauthorized');
}

const event = result.event;
console.log(`Verified ${event.type} for job ${event.data.jobId}`);
return res.status(200).send('OK');
```

### Verification parameters

| Option | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `payload` | `string \| Uint8Array` | **Yes** | The unparsed raw HTTP request body string or buffer. |
| `headers` | `Record \| Headers` | **Yes** | Incoming request headers containing `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature`. |
| `secret` | `string \| string[]` | **Yes** | Your workspace default webhook secret or endpoint secret (`whsec_...`). Also accepts an array of secrets. |
| `previousSecret` | `string` | No | Your previous secret during the 24-hour secret rotation grace period. |
| `toleranceSeconds` | `number` | No | Maximum allowable clock drift in seconds (default: `300`). Pass negative value to disable. |

### Return value

Returns a promise resolving to `WebhookVerifyResult`:
- `valid`: `true` if signature and timestamp are authentic, `false` otherwise.
- `error`: Error code if invalid (`'missing_headers'`, `'invalid_format'`, `'timestamp_out_of_range'`, `'signature_mismatch'`).
- `event`: Parsed JSON event object if `valid === true`.

---

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/sdk/python

Summary: Official atlascompiler package for Python applications, AI agents, and RAG data pipelines.

The official `atlascompiler` Python SDK provides a modern, type-annotated client powered by `httpx`. It is designed for seamless integration with Python AI workflows, LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, and FastAPI backends.

## Initialization

Initialize the `AtlasClient`. Credentials are automatically resolved from the `ATLAS_API_KEY` environment variable if not passed explicitly:

```python

from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

# Reads ATLAS_API_KEY from environment automatically
client = AtlasClient()

# Or pass explicitly:
client = AtlasClient(api_key="atlas_...", timeout=30.0)
```

The client also supports the context manager pattern:

```python
with AtlasClient() as client:
    result = client.scrape({"url": "https://example.com"})
    print(result.value["data"]["markdown"])
```

---

## Core Operations

### 1. Scrape a URL

```python
result = client.scrape({
    "url": "https://news.ycombinator.com",
    "formats": ["markdown", "links"]
})

print("Title:", result.value["metadata"]["title"])
print("Markdown:\n", result.value["data"]["markdown"])
```

---

### 2. Compile Dynamic Pages & Tables

```python
result = client.compile({
    "url": "https://stripe.com/pricing",
    "cache": {"forceFresh": False}
})

print("Compiled Markdown:\n", result.value["markdown"])
```

---

### 3. Map Domain Topology

```python
result = client.map({
    "url": "https://docs.github.com",
    "limit": 100,
    "sitemap": "include"
})

print(f"Discovered {len(result.value['links'])} URLs:")
for link in result.value["links"]:
    print(" -", link["url"])
```

---

### 4. Asynchronous Crawls

```python
# 1. Create crawl job
crawl = client.create_crawl({
    "url": "https://docs.stripe.com",
    "maxPages": 50,
    "includePaths": ["/docs/**"],
})

job_id = crawl.value["id"]
print(f"Admitted crawl job: {job_id}")

# 2. Wait for completion using built-in helper
job = client.wait_for_job(job_id)

# 3. Retrieve compiled pages
if job["status"] == "ready":
    results = client.list_job_results(job_id, limit=50)
    for item in results.value["data"]:
        print(item["url"], "->", len(item["markdown"]))
```

---

## Error Handling

The SDK raises `AtlasError` (or `AtlasApiError`) containing RFC 9457 Problem Details:

```python
from atlascompiler import AtlasClient, AtlasError

client = AtlasClient()

try:
    client.compile({"url": "https://invalid-domain.example"})
except AtlasError as err:
    print(f"HTTP Status: {err.status}")
    print(f"Machine Code: {err.code}")
    print(f"Detail: {err.message}")
    print(f"Request ID: {err.request_id}")
    print(f"Retryable: {err.retryable}")
```

---

## Verifying webhook signatures

The Python SDK exports `verify_webhook_signature` to validate incoming Standard Webhooks requests from Atlas:

```python

from atlascompiler import verify_webhook_signature

# In your Flask, FastAPI, or Django webhook route:
result = verify_webhook_signature(
    payload=request.get_data(as_text=True),  # raw bytes or string
    headers=request.headers,                 # dictionary or mapping of headers
    secret=os.environ["ATLAS_WEBHOOK_SECRET"],
    previous_secret=os.getenv("ATLAS_OLD_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),  # optional 24h rotation support
    tolerance_seconds=300,                                  # 5-minute replay window (default: 300)
)

if not result.valid:
    print(f"Webhook verification rejected: {result.error}")
    raise ValueError("Invalid webhook signature")

event = result.event
print(f"Verified event {event['type']} for job {event['data']['jobId']}")
```

### Verification parameters

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `payload` | `str \| bytes` | **Yes** | The exact unparsed HTTP request body string or raw bytes. |
| `headers` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | **Yes** | Request headers dictionary containing `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature`. |
| `secret` | `str \| list[str]` | **Yes** | Primary webhook secret (`whsec_...`) or list of valid candidate secrets. |
| `previous_secret` | `str \| None` | No | Previous secret for zero-downtime 24-hour secret rotation. |
| `tolerance_seconds` | `int` | No | Maximum allowed clock skew in seconds (default: `300`). Pass negative value to disable. |

### Return value

Returns a `WebhookVerifyResult` named tuple / model:
- `result.valid`: Boolean indicating whether the signature and timestamp are valid.
- `result.error`: Error reason string if invalid (`"missing_headers"`, `"invalid_format"`, `"timestamp_out_of_range"`, `"signature_mismatch"`).
- `result.event`: Parsed event dictionary when `result.valid is True`.

---

## Go SDK

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/sdk/go

Summary: Official go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk package for high-concurrency Go microservices, scrapers, and agents.

The official Atlas Go SDK provides an idiomatic, context-aware, type-safe client with zero third-party dependencies outside the Go standard library.

## Installation

```bash
go get go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk
```

Requires **Go 1.22+**.

---

## Initialization

Initialize the client with your Atlas API key:

```go
package main

	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	// Initialize with API key (or reads ATLAS_API_KEY from environment)
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))
}
```

---

## Core Operations

### 1. Scrape a URL

```go
package main

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	client := atlas.New(os.Getenv("ATLAS_API_KEY"))

	result, meta, err := client.Scrape(ctx, atlas.ScrapeUrlRequest{
		Url: "https://news.ycombinator.com",
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	fmt.Printf("HTTP Status: %d (Replayed: %t)\n", meta.StatusCode, meta.Replayed)
	if result.Data.Markdown != nil {
		fmt.Println(*result.Data.Markdown)
	}
}
```

---

### 2. Compile Dynamic Web Pages & Tables

```go
result, _, err := client.Compile(ctx, atlas.CompileUrlRequest{
	Url: "https://stripe.com/pricing",
})
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}

if result.Response200 != nil {
	fmt.Println(result.Response200.Markdown)
}
```

---

### 3. Map Domain Topology

```go
limit := 50
mapRes, _, err := client.Map(ctx, atlas.MapUrlRequest{
	Url:   "https://docs.github.com",
	Limit: &limit,
})
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}

fmt.Printf("Discovered %d URLs\n", len(mapRes.Links))
for _, link := range mapRes.Links {
	fmt.Println(" -", link.Url)
}
```

---

### 4. Asynchronous Crawls & Job Polling

```go
// 1. Create crawl job
maxPages := 50
crawl, _, err := client.CreateCrawl(ctx, atlas.CreateCrawlRequest{
	Url:      "https://docs.stripe.com",
	MaxPages: &maxPages,
})
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}

jobID := crawl.Id
fmt.Printf("Crawl admitted: %s\n", jobID)

// 2. Poll status
for {
	job, _, err := client.GetJob(ctx, jobID)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	if job.Status == "ready" || job.Status == "failed" {
		break
	}
	time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
}

// 3. Retrieve results
results, _, err := client.ListJobResults(ctx, jobID, nil, nil)
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}

for _, item := range results.Data {
	if item.Url != nil {
		fmt.Println(*item.Url, "-> completed")
	}
}
```

---

## Error Handling

API errors implement Go's standard `error` interface and unmarshal into `*atlas.Problem` containing RFC 9457 details:

```go
var problem *atlas.Problem
if errors.As(err, &problem) {
	fmt.Printf("HTTP Status: %d\n", problem.Status)
	fmt.Printf("Code: %s\n", problem.Code)
	fmt.Printf("Detail: %s\n", problem.Detail)
	fmt.Printf("Request ID: %s\n", problem.RequestId)
	fmt.Printf("Retryable: %t\n", problem.Retryable)
}
```

---

## Verifying webhook signatures

The Go SDK provides `atlas.VerifyWebhook` and `atlas.VerifyWebhookSignature` to authenticate incoming Standard Webhooks requests from Atlas:

```go
package main

	"io"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"

	"go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk"
)

func handleWebhook(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "Cannot read request body", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}

	secret := os.Getenv("ATLAS_WEBHOOK_SECRET")

	// Verify Standard Webhooks signature against incoming headers
	result, err := atlas.VerifyWebhook(body, r.Header, secret)
	if err != nil || !result.Valid {
		log.Printf("Webhook rejected: %s (err: %v)", result.Error, err)
		http.Error(w, "Invalid signature", http.StatusUnauthorized)
		return
	}

	log.Printf("Received verified event: %v", result.Event["type"])
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}
```

### Advanced verification options

For dual-secret rotation or custom clock drift tolerance, use `atlas.VerifyWebhookSignature`:

```go
tolerance := 5 * time.Minute
result, err := atlas.VerifyWebhookSignature(atlas.WebhookVerifyOptions{
	Payload:        body,
	Headers:        r.Header,
	Secret:         os.Getenv("ATLAS_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),
	PreviousSecret: os.Getenv("ATLAS_OLD_WEBHOOK_SECRET"), // 24-hour secret rotation support
	Tolerance:      &tolerance,
})
```

### Return value

Returns `(*atlas.WebhookVerifyResult, error)`:
- `result.Valid`: `true` if valid, `false` otherwise.
- `result.Error`: Error reason string if invalid (`"missing_headers"`, `"invalid_format"`, `"timestamp_out_of_range"`, `"signature_mismatch"`).
- `result.Event`: Unmarshaled JSON event map (`map[string]any`) when valid.

---

## Model Context Protocol (MCP) Hub

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/mcp-overview

Summary: Equip AI coding assistants and autonomous agents with deterministic, token-efficient web compilation using the open Model Context Protocol.

> **Protocol Specification:** Model Context Protocol `2026-07-28`  
> **Server Package:** `@atlascompiler/mcp`  
> **Streamable HTTP Endpoint:** `https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp`

The **Atlas Model Context Protocol (MCP) server** gives LLMs, AI coding assistants (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, VS Code), and autonomous agent frameworks deterministic, token-budgeted access to the live web.

Rather than feeding raw, noisy HTML into your model's context window—which burns token budgets and causes hallucinations—Atlas compiles dynamic web pages and single-page applications (SPAs) into clean, visual Markdown, tabular data, and structured AST graphs before delivering them to your agent.

---

## Why Atlas for AI Agents?

```mermaid
graph TD
    User["Developer Prompt in Cursor / Claude"] --> Agent["AI Agent (Claude 3.7 / GPT-4o)"]
    Agent -->|"MCP Tool Call: atlas_compile"| AtlasMCP["Atlas MCP Server"]
    AtlasMCP -->|"Deterministic Edge Pipeline"| LiveWeb["Live Web (SPAs, Tables, Docs)"]
    LiveWeb -->|"Rendered HTML"| AtlasMCP
    AtlasMCP -->|"Clean Markdown + Token Budget"| Agent
    Agent -->|"Accurate Synthesis"| User
```

Traditional web scrapers and browser-use tools return messy raw DOM trees, cookies banners, and thousands of lines of JavaScript bundles. Atlas solves the core failure modes of agentic web access:

1. **Token Tax Elimination**: Atlas eliminates 60% to 80% of unnecessary markup, headers, navigation chrome, and tracking scripts, returning only semantically relevant Markdown.
2. **Context Window Protection**: Every Atlas MCP tool enforces character budgets (`max_output_chars`). If a document exceeds the budget, Atlas cleanly truncates the text and returns navigable `atlas://` resource links so the agent never overflows its context window.
3. **Table & Code Precision**: Complex multi-column tables are compiled into GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) pipe tables, and syntax-highlighted code fences preserve indentation and language tags.
4. **Zero Data Retention (ZDR)**: Atlas does not retain compiled web content or LLM prompts on disk. Workflows operating on sensitive corporate documentation remain strictly private.

---

## 1-Click Interactive Setup

Run the official interactive setup wizard in your terminal. It detects your installed AI editors, prompts for your Atlas API key, and automatically merges the server configuration into your local editor settings:

The wizard supports the following options:

```bash
# Configure user-level settings globally across all projects
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --global

# Configure project-level settings (.cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json)
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --project

# Verify currently resolved credentials and active configuration
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp whoami
```

---

## Dual-Transport Architecture

Atlas MCP supports both standard transports specified by the Model Context Protocol:

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │             AI Client / IDE            │
                      │  (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf)    │
                      └──────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                         │
                   ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
                   │                                           │
         [Local Stdio Transport]                     [Streamable HTTP]
                   │                                           │
                   ▼                                           ▼
      ┌─────────────────────────┐               ┌─────────────────────────────┐
      │  @atlascompiler/mcp CLI  │               │ POST /mcp                   │
      │  (npx -y @atlas...)     │               │ https://api.atlas-compiler...│
      └────────────┬────────────┘               └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                   │                                           │
                   └─────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                            ┌────────────────────────┐
                            │    Atlas Edge Engine   │
                            └────────────────────────┘
```

| Transport | Primary Use Case | Connection Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **stdio Transport** | Local desktop editors (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, VS Code) | Run via `npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp` as a subprocess. Resolves credentials from `~/.atlas/credentials.json` or `ATLAS_API_KEY`. |
| **Streamable HTTP** | Cloud agents, serverless runners, LangGraph, CrewAI, Docker containers | Direct HTTP `POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer `. Stateless and horizontally scalable. |

---

## Capabilities Support Matrix

Atlas implements the complete Model Context Protocol `2026-07-28` specification:

| Capability | Status | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tools** | **Supported** | 5 deterministic web extraction tools (`atlas_scrape`, `atlas_compile`, `atlas_map`, `atlas_crawl`, `atlas_batch_compile`). |
| **Resources** | **Supported** | Virtual `atlas://` URI scheme providing lazy access to compilation artifacts, full ASTs, and crawl pagination. |
| **Prompts** | **Supported** | Pre-built prompts for documentation synthesis, competitor analysis, and API reverse-engineering. |
| **OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource** | **Supported** | RFC 8414 resource server metadata exposed at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. |
| **Security & Host Validation** | **Enforced** | Strict Host and Origin header validation to protect against DNS rebinding attacks. |

---

## Native MCP Tools Summary

Atlas exposes 5 core tools designed specifically for LLM tool calling:

| Tool Name | Operation | When to Use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`atlas_scrape`](/ai/tools-reference#atlas-scrape) | Fast-path single-page extraction | Quick retrieval of blogs, news articles, and simple documentation pages with minimal latency. |
| [`atlas_compile`](/ai/tools-reference#atlas-compile) | Visual layout compilation | Complex layouts, SPAs, pricing matrices, and technical documentation where table structure is critical. |
| [`atlas_map`](/ai/tools-reference#atlas-map) | High-speed URL topology mapping | Discovering site architecture, XML sitemaps, and documentation links without downloading page bodies. |
| [`atlas_crawl`](/ai/tools-reference#atlas-crawl) | Recursive multi-page spidering | Crawling multi-page documentation sections with include and exclude glob patterns. |
| [`atlas_batch_compile`](/ai/tools-reference#atlas-batch-compile) | Parallel multi-URL compilation | Compiling up to 20 URLs simultaneously with per-page budget enforcement and error isolation. |

## Cursor Setup & Agent Workflows

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/cursor

Summary: Connect Atlas MCP to Cursor IDE for real-time web compilation, API documentation research, and codebase synthesis.

Cursor supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling its Composer and Chat agents to directly call external tools during code generation and debugging. 

By connecting Atlas to Cursor, your agent can compile live web pages, read documentation sites, extract accurate pricing tables, and inspect sitemaps without leaving your editor.

---

## 1-Click Interactive Setup

The fastest way to configure Cursor is with the Atlas MCP setup wizard:

To configure Cursor specifically:

```bash
# Global configuration (available in all Cursor workspaces)
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --global

# Project-level configuration (committed to your repository)
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --project
```

The wizard validates your Atlas API key against `https://api.atlas-compiler.com/v1/health` and automatically merges the configuration into your Cursor settings file.

---

## Manual Configuration

If you prefer manual configuration, add the Atlas server to your Cursor MCP settings.

### File Locations

- **Global Configuration:**  
  - macOS & Linux: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`  
  - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json`
- **Project Configuration:**  
  - `.cursor/mcp.json` in your repository root.

### Configuration Format

Add the following block to your `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlas": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@atlascompiler/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "ATLAS_API_KEY": "atlas_your_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  Cursor automatically restarts active MCP servers when you save changes to `mcp.json`. You can verify connection status in Cursor under **Settings > Features > MCP**.

---

## Installing the Atlas Agent Skill

Cursor agents discover custom skills defined in your workspace or global configuration. Install the canonical Atlas Agent Skill to teach Cursor how to select the best Atlas tools automatically:

```bash
# Install to current project (.agents/skills/atlas/SKILL.md)
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp skill

# Install globally (~/.agents/skills/atlas/SKILL.md)
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp skill --global
```

The skill provides Cursor with zero-shot decision playbooks for web extraction, preventing unnecessary browser automation and token waste.

## Agent Prompt Recipes & Workflows

Once installed, Cursor Chat and Composer have access to all 5 Atlas tools (`atlas_scrape`, `atlas_compile`, `atlas_map`, `atlas_crawl`, `atlas_batch_compile`).

### 1. Compile Live Documentation for Code Generation

Instruct Cursor to fetch the latest SDK documentation before writing integration code:

```text
@atlas compile https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create and implement a TypeScript function to create a recurring subscription with metadata.
```

**Why this works**: Instead of relying on training data that might be out of date, Cursor calls `atlas_compile`, receives clean GFM Markdown with exact parameter tables and types, and generates accurate, hallucination-free code.

---

### 2. Map Site Architecture & Discover Endpoints

Before building a scraper or reverse-engineering a public service, map the target domain:

```text
@atlas map https://docs.github.com/en/rest and list all URL endpoints related to GitHub Actions webhooks.
```

**Why this works**: `atlas_map` inspects XML sitemaps and root HTML link topologies at edge speed, returning structured URL lists without downloading heavy page bodies.

---

### 3. Spider Multi-Page Documentation

When refactoring or upgrading a library across multiple documentation pages:

```text
@atlas crawl https://nextjs.org/docs with maxPages 5 and includePaths ["/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/**"] to explain how parallel routes work.
```

**Why this works**: Cursor triggers `atlas_crawl`, which compiles the relevant subset of pages and passes structured summaries back to the LLM context.

---

### 4. Extract Tabular Data & Pricing Matrices

```text
@atlas compile https://openai.com/api/pricing/ and write a TypeScript type definition and rate card for all GPT-4o models.
```

**Why this works**: Atlas compiles complex dynamic tables into exact GFM pipe tables, preserving row and column relationships that raw HTML scrapers scramble.

---

## Cursor Best Practices

  **Context Window Management**: Atlas automatically truncates large documents at `max_output_chars` (default: 30,000 characters) and includes an `atlas://` resource URI. If you need a more concise response, instruct Cursor: `@atlas scrape https://example.com with max_output_chars 5000`.

  **Environment Variables**: Never commit your Atlas API key in `.cursor/mcp.json` if your repository is public. Instead, set the `ATLAS_API_KEY` environment variable in your shell profile (`~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`), and Atlas MCP CLI will automatically resolve it.

---

## Verifying Setup

1. Open Cursor and navigate to **Cursor Settings** (`Cmd+,` or `Ctrl+,`).
2. Search for **MCP**.
3. Confirm that `atlas` is listed with a green indicator showing **Connected**.
4. Open Cursor Chat (`Cmd+L` or `Ctrl+L`) and type:
   ```text
   Use @atlas to scrape https://example.com and tell me its title.
   ```
5. Cursor will show a tool call to `atlas_scrape` and display the compiled result.

## Claude Desktop Setup & Research Workflows

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/claude-desktop

Summary: Empower Claude Desktop with deterministic web compilation, research capabilities, and tabular data extraction using Atlas MCP.

Anthropic's Claude Desktop provides native support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). By connecting Atlas to Claude Desktop, Claude gains the ability to autonomously browse, compile, and analyze live web content, complex documentation, and dynamic SPAs without losing formatting or blowing token budgets.

## 1-Click Interactive Setup

The official Atlas setup wizard configures Claude Desktop automatically:

Run the command with the `--global` flag:

```bash
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --global
```

The wizard:
1. Prompts for your Atlas API key.
2. Locates your Claude Desktop configuration file.
3. Automatically inserts the `atlas` MCP server definition without overwriting other configured tools.
4. Validates connectivity with the Atlas API.

---

## Manual Configuration

To configure Claude Desktop manually, locate your configuration file based on your operating system:

| Operating System | Configuration File Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| **macOS** | `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` |
| **Windows** | `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` |
| **Linux** | `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` |

### Configuration File Content

Add the `atlas` server block under `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlas": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@atlascompiler/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "ATLAS_API_KEY": "atlas_your_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  If you have existing MCP servers in `claude_desktop_config.json`, simply add `"atlas"` alongside them inside the `"mcpServers"` object. Restart Claude Desktop after updating the file.

---

## Troubleshooting Node.js Path in Claude Desktop

On macOS and Linux, GUI applications like Claude Desktop often run in a minimal shell environment that might not include your custom Node.js path (especially when using version managers like `nvm`, `fnm`, or `asdf`).

If Claude Desktop displays a red error indicator for Atlas:

1. Determine the absolute path to `npx` in your terminal:
   ```bash
   which npx
   # Output example: /usr/local/bin/npx or ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.0.0/bin/npx
   ```
2. Replace `"command": "npx"` with the absolute path in `claude_desktop_config.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "atlas": {
         "command": "/usr/local/bin/npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@atlascompiler/mcp"],
         "env": {
           "ATLAS_API_KEY": "atlas_your_api_key_here"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
3. Restart Claude Desktop.

### Checking Claude Desktop Logs

If you encounter issues, inspect Claude's local MCP logs:
- **macOS:** `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp*.log`
- **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\logs\mcp*.log`

## Conversational Research Workflows

With Atlas connected, you can ask Claude to perform deep web research tasks directly in conversation:

### 1. Financial & Corporate Research

> "Use Atlas to compile the latest quarterly earnings release from https://investor.apple.com/... and extract the services revenue breakdown into a summary table comparing YoY growth."

**What happens**: Claude calls `atlas_compile`, which deterministically preserves financial tables with proper alignment, allowing Claude to calculate percentage variances with 100% data fidelity.

---

### 2. Multi-Source Technical Comparison

> "I want to compare the deployment options of Fly.io and Render. Use Atlas to scrape https://fly.io/docs/about/overview/ and https://render.com/docs/web-services, and synthesize their differences regarding persistent volumes and regional multi-cloud."

**What happens**: Claude calls `atlas_scrape` on both URLs sequentially, receiving clean Markdown without sidebar navigation or cookie banners, and performs an unbiased technical synthesis.

---

### 3. Exploring Large Site Topologies

> "Use Atlas to map https://docs.astronomer.io and identify all documentation guides related to Apache Airflow DAG authoring."

**What happens**: Claude calls `atlas_map`, receives the full URL graph and sitemap discovery results, filters for relevant paths, and proposes a tailored reading list.

---

## Token Efficiency & Privacy in Claude

- **Zero Data Retention (ZDR)**: Your browsing queries and compiled web documents are never stored or logged on disk by Atlas.
- **Token Budget Protection**: Claude's context window is protected by Atlas's automatic 30,000-character budgeting and heading extraction.
- **Deterministic Tables**: Unlike LLM-based web browsing which frequently misaligns table columns, Atlas's compiler reconstructs DOM table geometries into clean GFM pipe tables before Claude sees them.

---

## Windsurf (Codeium) Setup & Cascade Workflows

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/windsurf

Summary: Configure Atlas MCP with Windsurf IDE to empower Cascade agents with deterministic web extraction and real-time documentation retrieval.

Windsurf, developed by Codeium, natively supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in its autonomous **Cascade** agent. By connecting Atlas to Windsurf, Cascade can independently browse the web, compile external documentation, extract API references, and verify third-party interfaces while refactoring your code.

---

## 1-Click Interactive Setup

The official Atlas setup wizard configures Windsurf automatically:

Run the command with the `--global` flag:

```bash
npx -y @atlascompiler/mcp init --global
```

The wizard detects Windsurf's configuration directory, adds the `atlas` MCP server configuration, and verifies connectivity.

---

## Manual Configuration

To configure Windsurf manually, open or create the MCP configuration file:

### Configuration File Path

- **macOS & Linux:** `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`
- **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\mcp_config.json`

### Configuration Content

Add the `atlas` server definition under `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlas": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@atlascompiler/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "ATLAS_API_KEY": "atlas_your_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After updating the file, reload Windsurf or open the **Windsurf Settings > MCP** panel to verify that the Atlas server status is active.

---

## Cascade Agent Workflows

Cascade operates as an agentic pair-programmer capable of taking multi-step actions. Here are several workflows showcasing how Cascade leverages Atlas tools:

### 1. Zero-Shot Library Implementation

Instruct Cascade to reference current documentation when generating boilerplate:

```text
Cascade, create a client for the PostHog API using TypeScript. First use @atlas to compile https://posthog.com/docs/api/capture and ensure our event batching schema matches their official specifications.
```

**Workflow**:
1. Cascade calls `atlas_compile` to fetch the PostHog API specifications.
2. Atlas strips away navigation chrome, compiling the request schema and headers into GFM tables.
3. Cascade inspects the clean Markdown and writes the exact TypeScript interface without schema drift.

---

### 2. Multi-Page Framework Migration

When upgrading dependencies across breaking versions:

```text
We are migrating our routing layer to SvelteKit 2. Use @atlas to crawl https://svelte.dev/docs/kit with maxPages 10 and includePaths ["/docs/kit/load**"] to discover the exact breaking changes in server load functions.
```

**Workflow**:
1. Cascade invokes `atlas_crawl` with path filtering.
2. Atlas traverses the documentation section, compiling pages concurrently.
3. Cascade receives structured summaries and autonomously updates your codebase files.

---

### 3. Rapid Site Topology Discovery

```text
Use @atlas to map https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers and list all available model architecture documentation guides.
```

---

## Windsurf Best Practices

  **Keep Cascade Focused**: Provide specific target URLs to Cascade when prompting. While Cascade can navigate links using `atlas_map`, providing a direct documentation URL alongside `@atlas compile` ensures the fastest turnaround.

  **API Key Security**: For shared projects, configure `ATLAS_API_KEY` in your personal environment variables rather than hardcoding it in repository-committed files. Atlas MCP CLI automatically falls back to environment variables.
