## MCP Tools Reference

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/tools-reference

Summary: Comprehensive parameter schemas, return types, and usage examples for all 5 native Atlas Model Context Protocol tools.

The Atlas Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes 5 core tools for LLM tool calling. Each tool is built with strict parameter validation using Zod, context window protection via automatic character budgeting, and standardized error responses.

---

## Tool Selection Decision Matrix

Agents should consult this decision matrix to determine the most cost-effective and low-latency tool for any web task:

| User Intent | Tool | Latency | Primary Advantage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Read single article, blog post, or standard page | `atlas_scrape` | ~1.3s | Fast extraction with minimal overhead and optional link discovery. |
| Extract pricing matrices, complex tables, SPAs | `atlas_compile` | ~1.6s | Full deterministic layout compilation preserving GFM tables and AST graphs. |
| Map all URLs or discover sitemaps on a domain | `atlas_map` | ~800ms | Rapid link graph and XML sitemap discovery without downloading page content. |
| Spider multi-page documentation sections | `atlas_crawl` | Multi-page | Recursive traversal with path globs (`includePaths`) and bounded polling. |
| Compile a known list of 2–20 URLs in parallel | `atlas_batch_compile` | Parallel | Concurrent execution with isolated per-page error handling and budgets. |

---

## `atlas_scrape`

Fast-path single-page extraction with low latency and optional link discovery.

### Input Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `url` | `string` | **Yes** | — | The absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL to scrape. |
| `formats` | `string[]` | No | `["markdown"]` | Desired output formats: `"markdown"`, `"links"`, or `"text"`. |
| `max_output_chars` | `integer` | No | `30000` | Maximum character budget. If exceeded, content is cleanly sliced. |
| `timeout_ms` | `integer` | No | `30000` | Execution timeout in milliseconds (max: 60000). |

### Return Schema

```typescript
interface AtlasScrapeResult {
  url: string;
  title: string;
  markdown?: string;
  text?: string;
  links?: Array;
  stats: {
    character_count: number;
    word_count: number;
    read_time_seconds: number;
  };
  truncated: boolean;
}
```

### Example MCP Tool Call

```json
{
  "name": "atlas_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/announcement",
    "formats": ["markdown", "links"],
    "max_output_chars": 20000
  }
}
```

---

## `atlas_compile`

High-fidelity deterministic visual compiler. Preserves complex layout geometries, multi-column tables, syntax-highlighted code fences, and semantic document outlines.

### Input Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `url` | `string` | **Yes** | — | The absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL to compile. |
| `format` | `string` | No | `"markdown"` | Output format: `"markdown"`, `"semantic"` (includes AST), or `"markdown+links"`. |
| `max_output_chars` | `integer` | No | `30000` | Character budget (min: 1000, max: 200000). Content beyond budget is truncated with resource URIs. |
| `force_fresh` | `boolean` | No | `false` | When `true`, bypasses edge cache and forces a fresh compilation. |

### Return Schema

```typescript
interface AtlasCompileResult {
  url: string;
  compilation_id: string;
  title: string;
  markdown?: string;
  ast?: Record;
  headings?: Array;
  resources: {
    compiled_artifact_uri: string; // e.g. "atlas://compilations/comp_abc123"
    ast_uri?: string;              // e.g. "atlas://compilations/comp_abc123/ast"
  };
  stats: {
    character_count: number;
    tokens_saved_pct?: number;     // Average: 65% token tax elimination
    compilation_time_ms: number;
  };
  truncated: boolean;
}
```

### Example MCP Tool Call

```json
{
  "name": "atlas_compile",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://stripe.com/pricing",
    "format": "markdown",
    "max_output_chars": 50000
  }
}
```

---

## `atlas_map`

Sitemap-first domain topology discovery. Traverses XML sitemaps and HTML anchor graphs to map available URLs without downloading full page bodies.

### Input Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `url` | `string` | **Yes** | — | The root or entry URL of the domain to map. |
| `limit` | `integer` | No | `100` | Maximum number of URLs to return (1 to 10,000). |
| `include_subdomains` | `boolean` | No | `false` | When `true`, follows links across subdomains of the target. |
| `sitemap` | `string` | No | `"include"` | Sitemap discovery policy: `"include"`, `"skip"`, or `"only"`. |

### Return Schema

```typescript
interface AtlasMapResult {
  root_url: string;
  urls: string[];
  count: number;
  sitemaps_found: string[];
  duration_ms: number;
}
```

### Example MCP Tool Call

```json
{
  "name": "atlas_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://docs.github.com",
    "limit": 50,
    "sitemap": "include"
  }
}
```

---

## `atlas_crawl`

Recursive multi-page spidering with path filtering and depth control. Designed for documentation sets, knowledge bases, and multi-page technical guides.

### Input Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `url` | `string` | **Yes** | — | Root starting URL for the crawl. |
| `max_pages` | `integer` | No | `10` | Maximum number of pages to compile. |
| `max_depth` | `integer` | No | `2` | Maximum link traversal depth from root (1 to 10). |
| `include_paths` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Glob patterns to restrict crawl boundaries (e.g., `["/docs/**"]`). |
| `exclude_paths` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Glob patterns to omit from the crawl (e.g., `["/blog/archive/**"]`). |

### Return Schema

```typescript
interface AtlasCrawlResult {
  crawl_id: string;
  root_url: string;
  pages_crawled: number;
  pages_failed: number;
  summary_markdown: string;
  pages: Array;
  duration_ms: number;
}
```

### Bounded Polling Behavior

`atlas_crawl` implements **opportunistic bounded polling** up to 3 seconds:
- If the crawl completes within 3 seconds, all compiled page items are returned synchronously.
- If the crawl is still running, Atlas performs a clean asynchronous handoff, returning the `crawl_id` and a resource URI (`atlas://crawls/{crawl_id}`) so your agent does not hang.

---

## `atlas_batch_compile`

Parallel compilation of multiple URLs with per-page budget enforcement and isolated error resilience.

### Input Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `urls` | `string[]` | **Yes** | — | Array of 1 to 20 absolute URLs to compile in parallel. |
| `format` | `string` | No | `"markdown"` | Output format: `"markdown"`, `"semantic"`, or `"markdown+links"`. |
| `max_output_chars_per_page` | `integer` | No | `15000` | Per-page character budget to prevent context window overflow. |

### Return Schema

```typescript
interface AtlasBatchCompileResult {
  total_requested: number;
  successful: number;
  failed: number;
  results: Array;
}
```

### Example MCP Tool Call

```json
{
  "name": "atlas_batch_compile",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": [
      "https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome",
      "https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/models-overview",
      "https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/prompt-engineering"
    ],
    "max_output_chars_per_page": 10000
  }
}
```

---

## MCP Protocol & Wire Reference

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/protocol-reference

Summary: Technical wire specification for connecting to the Atlas Model Context Protocol server over Streamable HTTP and stdio transports.

Atlas implements the open **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** specification (`2026-07-28`), offering both local stdio execution and cloud-native **Streamable HTTP** ingress.

This reference provides technical details for developers integrating custom agent frameworks, building MCP client libraries, or inspecting JSON-RPC 2.0 wire traffic.

---

## Ingress Endpoints & Transport Modes

Atlas exposes two primary transports:

| Mode | Endpoint | Transport Protocol | Authentication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Streamable HTTP** | `POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp` | HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 POST with JSON-RPC 2.0 | `Authorization: Bearer ` |
| **stdio Transport** | CLI process via `@atlascompiler/mcp` | Standard input / standard output | Local credentials or `ATLAS_API_KEY` |

---

## Streamable HTTP Transport

The Streamable HTTP transport allows cloud-native AI agents and containerized microservices to communicate with Atlas without spawning local Node.js child processes.

### Required HTTP Headers

When issuing requests to `POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp`, include the following headers:

| Header | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Authorization` | `string` | **Required**. `Bearer `. |
| `Content-Type` | `string` | **Required**. Must be `application/json`. |
| `Accept` | `string` | Recommended. `application/json, text/event-stream`. |
| `Mcp-Method` | `string` | Optional routing hint matching the JSON-RPC method (e.g. `tools/call`, `tools/list`). |
| `Mcp-Name` | `string` | Optional routing hint matching the target tool name (e.g. `atlas_compile`). |

---

## RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata

Atlas exposes OAuth 2.0 resource server discovery metadata compliant with RFC 8414:

```http
GET https://api.atlas-compiler.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource HTTP/1.1
```

### Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "resource": "https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp",
  "authorization_servers": [
    "https://clerk.atlas-compiler.com"
  ],
  "scopes_supported": [
    "atlas:compile",
    "atlas:map",
    "atlas:crawl",
    "atlas:read_results"
  ]
}
```

---

## JSON-RPC 2.0 Protocol Lifecycle

All MCP communications follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

### 1. Initialization (`initialize`)

The client negotiates protocol capabilities with Atlas during connection startup.

#### Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "initialize",
  "params": {
    "protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
    "capabilities": {
      "roots": { "listChanged": true },
      "sampling": {}
    },
    "clientInfo": {
      "name": "my-custom-agent",
      "version": "1.0.0"
    }
  }
}
```

#### Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
    "capabilities": {
      "tools": {},
      "resources": {
        "subscribe": false,
        "listChanged": false
      },
      "prompts": {}
    },
    "serverInfo": {
      "name": "atlas",
      "version": "1.0.0"
    }
  }
}
```

---

### 2. Discover Tools (`tools/list`)

Returns all available Atlas compilation, scraping, mapping, and crawling tools along with their full Zod-generated JSON Schema definitions.

#### Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/list",
  "params": {}
}
```

---

### 3. Execute Tool (`tools/call`)

Executes a specific Atlas tool synchronously.

#### Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "atlas_compile",
    "arguments": {
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "format": "markdown",
      "max_output_chars": 25000
    }
  }
}
```

#### Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "# Example Domain\n\nThis domain is for use in documentation examples...\n\n---\n**Compilation ID:** `comp_018f2a1b9e00`\n**Resource URI:** `atlas://compilations/comp_018f2a1b9e00`"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

---

## Virtual Resource URI Schemes

Atlas exposes virtual resource templates via the `atlas://` URI scheme. When a compilation or crawl result exceeds an agent's character budget, the truncated output provides resource URIs for lazy retrieval.

| URI Template | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `atlas://compilations/{compilation_id}` | Full compiled Markdown document without truncation. |
| `atlas://compilations/{compilation_id}/ast` | Structured AST content graph as a JSON object. |
| `atlas://compilations/{compilation_id}/sections/{section_id}` | Individual section or heading block from the compiled document. |
| `atlas://crawls/{crawl_id}` | Paginated compilation manifest and page list for a crawl job. |

### Reading a Resource (`resources/read`)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "resources/read",
  "params": {
    "uri": "atlas://compilations/comp_018f2a1b9e00"
  }
}
```

---

## Security & DNS Rebinding Defenses

Atlas implements strict host and origin filtering to defend against DNS rebinding attacks:

1. **Host Header Validation**: Requests to `POST /mcp` must present an allowed Host header (`api.atlas-compiler.com`). Unrecognized or remapped Host headers are rejected with `403 Forbidden`.
2. **Origin Header Enforcement**: For browser-based MCP clients, only approved Atlas web domains and local developer origins (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) are permitted. Non-browser clients (which omit `Origin`) pass unimpeded.
3. **Stateless Ingress**: Non-POST/OPTIONS requests (such as `GET /mcp`) are explicitly rejected with `405 Method Not Allowed`, ensuring client implementations do not assume stateful long-lived HTTP socket sessions.

---

## Agent Framework Integrations

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/ai/agent-frameworks

Summary: Build custom LLM agents and multi-agent systems using Atlas with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, and CrewAI.

While desktop AI IDEs connect to Atlas via local stdio or pre-configured MCP clients, autonomous cloud agents, RAG pipelines, and multi-agent swarms integrate using official SDKs or direct tool declarations.

This guide provides tested recipes for integrating Atlas web compilation into popular AI frameworks.

---

## Vercel AI SDK (`ai`)

Use the official `@atlascompiler/sdk` to define deterministic web extraction tools in Next.js or Node.js agent workflows:

```typescript

const atlas = new AtlasClient({
  apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY!,
});

const atlasCompileTool = tool({
  description: 'Compile a live web page or documentation into clean, token-efficient Markdown.',
  parameters: z.object({
    url: z.string().url().describe('The URL of the webpage to compile'),
  }),
  execute: async ({ url }) => {
    const result = await atlas.compile({ url });
    return {
      title: result.metadata?.title,
      markdown: result.data.markdown,
    };
  },
});

export async function runResearchAgent(prompt: string) {
  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: openai('gpt-4o'),
    tools: {
      compileWebPage: atlasCompileTool,
    },
    maxSteps: 3,
    prompt,
  });

  return text;
}
```

---

## LangChain & LangGraph

```python Python (LangChain)

from langchain.tools import tool
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

@tool
def compile_webpage(url: str) -> str:
    """Compile a live web page or SPA into token-efficient Markdown."""
    response = atlas.compile(url=url)
    return response.data.markdown

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0)
tools = [compile_webpage]
llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(tools)

query = "What are the latest enterprise pricing options on https://example.com/pricing?"
messages = [("human", query)]
ai_msg = llm_with_tools.invoke(messages)
```

```typescript TypeScript (LangChain)

const atlas = new AtlasClient({ apiKey: process.env.ATLAS_API_KEY! });

const compileTool = tool(
  async ({ url }) => {
    const res = await atlas.compile({ url });
    return res.data.markdown;
  },
  {
    name: "compile_webpage",
    description: "Compile a live URL into clean LLM-ready Markdown",
    schema: z.object({
      url: z.string().url(),
    }),
  }
);

const model = new ChatOpenAI({ model: "gpt-4o" }).bindTools([compileTool]);
```

---

## LlamaIndex

Build RAG pipelines that ingest live, deterministic Markdown directly into vector index documents without running headless browser containers:

```python

from llama_index.core import Document, VectorStoreIndex
from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

def load_web_documents(urls: list[str]) -> list[Document]:
    documents = []
    for url in urls:
        response = atlas.compile(url=url)
        doc = Document(
            text=response.data.markdown,
            metadata={
                "url": response.metadata.canonical_url or url,
                "title": response.metadata.title,
                "status_code": response.metadata.status_code,
            },
        )
        documents.append(doc)
    return documents

# Ingest and query
docs = load_web_documents(["https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome"])
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
answer = query_engine.query("What are the core capabilities described in these docs?")
print(answer)
```

---

## CrewAI

Equip autonomous agent swarms with Atlas web intelligence tools:

```python

from crewai.tools import tool
from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew
from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

@tool("Compile Web Content")
def compile_web_content(url: str) -> str:
    """Useful to extract clean, visual Markdown from any public URL or SPA."""
    res = atlas.compile(url=url)
    return res.data.markdown

researcher = Agent(
    role="Senior Market Analyst",
    goal="Extract and synthesize competitive feature matrices from competitor websites",
    backstory="You are an expert researcher specialized in SaaS architecture and pricing strategies.",
    tools=[compile_web_content],
    verbose=True,
)

research_task = Task(
    description="Compile https://stripe.com/pricing and summarize their interchange plus rates.",
    expected_output="A structured table comparing standard and custom enterprise pricing.",
    agent=researcher,
)

crew = Crew(agents=[researcher], tasks=[research_task])
result = crew.kickoff()
print(result)
```

---

## Direct OpenAI Function Calling

If you are using raw HTTP requests or the official OpenAI SDK without a higher-level framework:

```python

from openai import OpenAI
from atlascompiler import AtlasClient

openai_client = OpenAI()
atlas = AtlasClient(api_key=os.environ["ATLAS_API_KEY"])

tools = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "compile_webpage",
            "description": "Compile a live URL into clean Markdown",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "url": {"type": "string", "description": "Target webpage URL"}
                },
                "required": ["url"],
            },
        },
    }
]

response = openai_client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is the headline at https://news.ycombinator.com?"}],
    tools=tools,
)

tool_call = response.choices[0].message.tool_calls[0]
if tool_call.function.name == "compile_webpage":
    args = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)
    compiled = atlas.compile(url=args["url"])
    print("Compiled Web Content:\n", compiled.data.markdown[:500])
```

## Product Changelog

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/changelog/overview

Summary: Release notes, platform updates, and feature announcements for the Atlas web compiler and developer platform.

Track updates, new capabilities, and platform releases across the Atlas API, official SDKs, and Model Context Protocol integrations.

---

## Atlas v1.0.0 — Launch Release

Welcome to the initial production release of **Atlas Compiler** (`v1.0.0`). Atlas delivers a deterministic visual Web-to-Markdown compiler built from the ground up for LLM reasoning and autonomous AI agents.

### Core Compiler & Extraction Engine

- **Visual Edge Compilation (`POST /v1/compile`)**:
  - Deterministic conversion of dynamic SPAs, complex documentation layouts, and multi-column tables into clean, token-efficient GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM).
  - Eliminates 60% to 80% of unnecessary markup, headers, and tracking noise compared to raw HTML extractors.
  - Optional Intermediate Representation (`ir`) format for structured AST graph traversal and semantic hierarchy inspection.
- **Fast Single-Page Scraper (`POST /v1/scrape`)**:
  - Low-latency extraction of Markdown, links, and page metadata for lightweight content retrieval.
  - In-memory processing with audited **Zero Data Retention (ZDR)**—no target page bodies or user content are retained on disk.

### Multi-Page Exploration & Discovery

- **Domain Topology Mapping (`POST /v1/map`)**:
  - Fast sitemap-first URL discovery and heuristic route prioritization (0–100 scoring) without downloading full page bodies.
  - Estimates total page count, primary framework, language, and token budget across the target domain.
- **Distributed Recursive Crawler (`POST /v1/crawls`)**:
  - Asynchronous multi-page spidering with glob path filtering (`includePaths`, `excludePaths`), depth limits, and max page caps.
  - Opportunistic bounded polling for instant responses on smaller crawl targets.
- **Resilient Batch Processing (`POST /v1/batches`)**:
  - Parallel compilation of up to 1,000 explicit URLs per job with partial failure isolation—individual upstream errors do not abort the job.

### Model Context Protocol (MCP 2026-07-28)

- **Official `@atlascompiler/mcp` Server**:
  - Implements the open Model Context Protocol `2026-07-28` specification.
  - Dual-transport architecture: local stdio process for Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, and VS Code; cloud-native Streamable HTTP at `POST https://api.atlas-compiler.com/mcp`.
  - 5 agent-ready tools: `atlas_compile`, `atlas_scrape`, `atlas_map`, `atlas_crawl`, and `atlas_batch`.
  - Context window protection via character budgets and virtual `atlas://` resource URIs (`compilation`, `section`, `ast`, `crawl`).
  - RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource discovery at `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

### Developer Platform & SDKs

- **Multi-Language Client Libraries**:
  - **TypeScript / JavaScript**: `@atlascompiler/sdk` with full typing, response envelope convenience getters, and HMAC signature helpers.
  - **Python**: `atlascompiler` on PyPI with synchronous and asynchronous clients, typed models, and keyword argument flexibility.
  - **Go**: `go.atlas-compiler.com/sdk` with zero external dependencies outside standard library and context cancellation.
- **Cryptographic Webhooks**:
  - Real-time HMAC-SHA256 signed event delivery for asynchronous crawl and batch completion (`crawl.completed`, `batch.completed`, `crawl.failed`, `batch.failed`).
- **Production Quotas & Problem Details**:
  - Machine-readable RFC 9457 error details with granular `code`, `requestId`, and `retryable` indicators.
  - Concurrency leasing and credit consumption management powered by D1 compare-and-swap invariants.

---

## API Stability & Deprecation Policy

URL: https://docs.atlas-compiler.com/changelog/api-stability

Summary: Atlas API versioning commitments, backwards compatibility guarantees, breaking change windows, and deprecation headers.

Atlas is designed for mission-critical software pipelines. We adhere to strict API stability guarantees to ensure that updates and enhancements do not break running client applications or production workflows.

---

## Semantic Versioning Guarantees

All public REST endpoints are namespaced by major version (`/v1`). 

### Backward-Compatible Changes (Non-Breaking)

The following changes may occur without notice and are considered non-breaking:
- Adding new optional request parameters or headers.
- Adding new properties to existing JSON response objects.
- Introducing new API endpoints or HTTP methods.
- Adding new error codes or expanding error descriptions.
- Adding new enum values to non-constrained response fields.

  **Client Parsing Guidance**: Clients should ignore unrecognized properties in response JSON payloads rather than failing deserialization.

---

### Breaking Changes & Major Versions

Any change that would break compliant client implementations will only be introduced in a new major version (e.g. `/v2`):
- Removing or renaming an existing endpoint.
- Making an optional request parameter required.
- Modifying the type or meaning of an existing request or response field.
- Changing the cryptographic signature format of webhooks.

---

## Deprecation Process & Notice Period

In the rare event that an endpoint or feature is marked for deprecation:

1. **6-Month Minimum Notice**: Features slated for deprecation will remain functional in production for a minimum of **6 months** following formal deprecation announcement.
2. **Deprecation Headers**: Deprecated endpoints will return standardized HTTP response headers:
   - `Deprecation: @` (RFC 8594)
   - `Sunset: ` indicating the scheduled termination date.
   - `Link: ; rel="sunset"` linking to migration documentation.
3. **Dashboard & Email Alerts**: Workspace owners will receive proactive notifications regarding any active API keys issuing calls to deprecated routes.

---

## Machine-Readable Contract Evolution

The canonical definition of the Atlas public API is published as `atlas.openapi.json`. Every pull request and release in our automated CI/CD pipeline validates that existing schemas remain backward-compatible before deployment.

---
